A1.justification: Both PDFs describe A3D and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The shared method and experiments can be matched reliably despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation and transformation measurements in Tables 1–3, alongside hybridization examples and qualitative ablations.

after.justification: v2 reports original comparative experiments, quantitative ablations, and RichDreamer-based results in Tables 1–7 and associated figures.

M1.justification: v2 adds a substantive RichDreamer-based implementation using DMTet/SDF geometry, staged geometry and texture optimization, and normal-depth/albedo guidance (Appendices A and B.2). The core simplex interpolation, hybridization, and source-anchored editing procedures remain. Its main method description also emphasizes depth and normal-map regularization instead of v1's explicit spectral normalization, although removal of spectral normalization is not explicitly confirmed.

E1.justification: The three tasks and 15 joint-generation prompt pairs remain, including plants already evaluated in v1. Demonstrated coverage contracts slightly: the plant-decoration editing case in v1 Table 2 and mosquito/wasp hybridization example in Figure 8 are absent from v2. RichDreamer adds a model configuration rather than new data coverage.

E2.justification: v1 primarily compares against MVEdit. v2 adds LucidDreamer and GaussianEditor to aligned generation. Editing adds GaussianEditor quantitatively and LucidDreamer through qualitative comparisons and successful per-case results in Table 6; LucidDreamer's failures prevent an aggregate comparison in Table 2.

E3.justification: v2 replaces Chamfer distance with normalized DIFT correspondence distance and adds six GPT-4o evaluation criteria using 90 comparisons per method pair. The editing table changes from 24 cases to 26, and new backbone and ablation configurations are evaluated. CLIP averaging over 120 views is retained.

E4.justification: v1's ablation qualitatively compares separate networks, a shared network without interpolation, and the full method. v2 adds empty-prompt transition guidance and network-depth controls, with aggregate and per-pair quantitative results in Tables 3 and 7. Appendix A additionally tests generalization to the RichDreamer backbone.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or significance tests. v2's 90 GPT-based comparisons specify evaluation sample size, without adding uncertainty estimates or establishing repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Reported aligned-generation CLIP averages change from A3D/MVEdit 29.46/27.92 to 27.7/27.1; editing averages change from 29.56/28.76 to 27.8/27.9. Revised methods and evaluation prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. v2 also adds extensive DIFT, GPT-based, ablation, and RichDreamer results, while removing some qualitative examples.

T1.justification: v2 defines a normalized, bidirectional DIFT correspondence distance mathematically in Appendix C, adding a formal metric construction absent from v1. The existing NeRF, SDS, and simplex formulations remain substantially unchanged, and neither version develops theorem-and-proof results.

C1.justification: The central contribution—joint generation of aligned objects enabling hybridization and structure-preserving editing—remains. v2 adds explicit claims about the necessity of transition plausibility and smoothness and effectiveness across backbones. Its introduction and conclusion qualify editing performance as on par with specialized methods, whereas v1 claims superiority in quality and semantic alignment.

C2.justification: v2 substantially develops the mechanism interpretation, separating plausibility regularization from prompt blending and discussing an alignment-versus-realism tradeoff. It explains why limited geometric editing can obtain favorable DIFT scores and discusses backbone-specific weaknesses. The static-object limitation remains, while v1's explicit warning about substantially different proportions is removed.

D1.justification: New Appendices B and C provide architecture, hash-grid, latent-sampling, regularization-weight, initialization, baseline-adaptation, and evaluation details. Examples include 0.5 probability of individual-object sampling, RichDreamer network specifications, MVEdit denoising strength, and the CLIP ViT-L/14 model. These greatly expand v1's sparse implementation information; newly disclosed settings do not establish changes to earlier experiments.

R1.justification: v2 removes the broad 2D diffusion survey, expands discussion of 3D editing and amortized generation, and adds a dedicated latent-space regularization subsection. Connections to StyleGAN and adversarial interpolation substantially develop the methodological positioning. RichDreamer was already cited in v1; its new experimental use is a separate change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, and experimental discussion are extensively rewritten. Terminology shifts toward structural alignment and latent codes, metrics receive a shared explanation, and the single additional-results appendix becomes four focused appendices. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns comparison figures to include more methods and separate appearance/geometry views, expands the ablation display, and adds a RichDreamer figure. The combined comparison table becomes separate task tables with additional metrics. Existing hybridization examples are condensed and rearranged, while v1's trajectory Figures 3 and 10 are omitted.

improvement.justification: v1's limited comparator coverage, qualitative-only ablations, and sparse implementation information leave important validation and reproducibility gaps. v2 substantially addresses these through additional baselines, quantitative component controls, a second implementation, and detailed appendices. Some illustrative examples disappear and uncertainty remains unreported, but the stronger experimental support and technical transparency provide a clear overall improvement despite mixed performance results.
